# Cipherati Full Knowledge Digest & LLM System Prompt Context
Website: https://cipherati.com/
Publisher: Cipherati Intelligence Desk

## About Cipherati
Cipherati is an independent, practitioner-grade radar of battle-tested AI developer tools, coding agents, and production systems — combined with real-time cybersecurity news, statutory threat provenance, and citizen scam defense intelligence. Zero vendor hype.

## 2. Citizen Scam Defense Playbooks (19 Verified Modus Operandi)

### Scam #1: The "Digital Arrest" Police Video Call
- Platform: WhatsApp / Video Call
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: A caller in uniform claims your Aadhaar or passport was found in an illegal parcel or money laundering probe. They place you on a fraudulent WhatsApp video call or custom video link with a backdrop resembling a police station, CBI, or ED cyber cell, declaring you are under 'Digital Arrest' and coercing you to transfer savings into a fake 'RBI verification escrow'.
- Defense Rule: Indian law and law enforcement agencies have NO legal concept of 'Digital Arrest'. Police, CBI, ED, and customs NEVER conduct interrogations, trials, or arrests over video calls. Hang up immediately, block the number, and report to the National Cybercrime Portal or dial 1930.
- Statutory Authority: I4C & PM Mann Ki Baat Cyber Alert (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #2: The Fake Traffic Fine Message (e-Challan APK)
- Platform: SMS / Android APK
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: You get an SMS claiming your vehicle was caught overspeeding on camera with a pending fine of ₹1,000, and a link to download an app (echallan.apk) to pay before court action. If you install it, the app silently reads all your incoming SMS, steals your bank OTPs, and drains your account.
- Defense Rule: Traffic police never send app files to pay fines. Never install any file ending in .apk. Always check and pay traffic fines only on the official government website: echallan.parivahan.gov.in.
- Statutory Authority: I4C (Ministry of Home Affairs) Cyber Alert (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #3: The WhatsApp "Wedding Card" Virus (APK Trojan)
- Platform: WhatsApp / Android APK
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: You receive a message from a friend or relative on WhatsApp saying: "My cousin is getting married next week, wedding card and venue attached." The attached file looks like an invite, but ends in .apk. Installing it infects your phone with a virus that hijacks your WhatsApp, sends the same scam to all your family contacts, and steals your net banking logins.
- Defense Rule: Real wedding cards are always photos or PDFs, never an .apk software file. If someone sends an APK file, do not tap it. Call that person on a regular call to tell them their WhatsApp is compromised.
- Statutory Authority: CERT-In Cyber Security Advisory (https://www.cert-in.org.in/)

### Scam #4: The "Wrong UPI Transfer" Crying Call
- Platform: UPI / Phone Call
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You get a genuine bank alert that ₹30,000 was credited to your account. Seconds later, a crying person calls saying: "Sir, my child is in the hospital, I sent money to your number by mistake. Please send it back to my UPI ID." If you send the money back yourself, you lose your own money—because the original transfer was made using stolen funds. Within 48 hours, cyber police freeze your bank account for receiving criminal money.
- Defense Rule: Never transfer the money back yourself. Tell the caller: "I will not touch this money. Please call your bank and file a wrong-transfer dispute. My bank will reverse it officially."
- Statutory Authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Sachet Advisory) (https://sachet.rbi.org.in/)

### Scam #5: The Fake QR Code "To Receive Payment" Trap
- Platform: OLX / UPI QR Code
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You list furniture or a vehicle for sale on OLX or Marketplace. A buyer immediately agrees to the price without negotiation and sends you a UPI QR code saying: "Scan this QR code and enter your UPI PIN to receive the advance payment of ₹15,000." The moment you enter your PIN, ₹15,000 is debited from your account.
- Defense Rule: Remember the golden rule of UPI: You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN or scan a QR code to RECEIVE money. Entering a PIN is only required when money leaves your bank account.
- Statutory Authority: NPCI & National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (https://www.npci.org.in/)

### Scam #6: The "5G Plus Upgrade" Number Steal
- Platform: eSIM / SMS
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: A caller claiming to be from Airtel or Jio says they are upgrading your SIM to 5G for free. They tell you to send a simple SMS like eSIM <email> to 121. The moment you do this, your physical SIM card stops working permanently, and your phone number transfers to the scammer's phone. All your bank SMS OTPs now go to them.
- Defense Rule: Never send an eSIM request to any email given by a caller. Telecom companies never call you to set up an eSIM. To upgrade your SIM, always visit an official Airtel/Jio store in person.
- Statutory Authority: DoT (Department of Telecommunications) / Sanchar Saathi (https://sancharsaathi.gov.in/)

### Scam #7: The FASTag Highway Blacklist Trap
- Platform: SMS / Web Clone
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You get an urgent SMS saying your FASTag is blacklisted or KYC is expired, demanding a ₹45 pending fee within 2 hours or your vehicle will be stopped at the next toll plaza. The link opens a fake cloned website that captures your bank account and debit card details.
- Defense Rule: Highway authorities never send SMS links to collect ₹45 or update KYC. Never click links in SMS. If you want to check your FASTag, open your own banking app or Paytm directly.
- Statutory Authority: NPCI & Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (https://www.npci.org.in/)

### Scam #8: The "Look-Alike Voice" AI Deepfake Distress Call
- Platform: Phone Call / Audio AI
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: An elderly parent receives a call that sounds identically like their son or daughter crying in panic: "Dad, I was in a car crash / police detained me, please send ₹50,000 to this inspector's UPI immediately to avoid lockup." The voice is an AI clone generated from a 5-second public Instagram clip.
- Defense Rule: Establish a family secret safe-word. Never transfer money under emotional pressure. Hang up immediately and dial your child's number directly on a normal voice call or video call.
- Statutory Authority: CERT-In AI Threat Advisory (https://cert-in.org.in/)

### Scam #9: The Fake Electricity Bill Disconnection Warning
- Platform: SMS / Remote App
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You get an urgent SMS: "Dear consumer, your electricity connection will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM due to unpaid balance. Call power officer immediately." If you call, they tell you to install QuickSupport or AnyDesk to pay ₹11 for KYC update, which gives them full control to drain your bank account.
- Defense Rule: Power boards never threaten same-night power cuts over SMS or ask you to call personal mobile numbers. Never install screen-sharing apps on advice from a stranger. Pay bills only via authorized electricity board portals.
- Statutory Authority: Ministry of Power & I4C Advisory (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #10: The WhatsApp Part-Time "Hotel Review / Like" Job
- Platform: WhatsApp / Telegram
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You get a WhatsApp message offering ₹2,000–₹5,000 per day to like YouTube videos or review hotels. You complete initial tasks and receive ₹300 genuine payout to build trust. Then you are added to a Telegram VIP group and convinced to deposit ₹50,000 to "unlock" higher commissions, which you can never withdraw.
- Defense Rule: Legitimate businesses never recruit over WhatsApp to pay for video likes. Any scheme paying small token amounts upfront to lure you into depositing larger "prepaid" funds is a scam.
- Statutory Authority: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #11: The DoT / TRAI "Mobile Number Disconnection in 2 Hours" Robocall
- Platform: Phone Call / Robocall IVR
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: An automated IVR robocall says: "This is the Department of Telecommunications (DoT). Your mobile number will be disconnected in 2 hours due to illegal cybercrime complaints. Press 9 to speak with an officer." Pressing 9 routes you to fake police who threaten immediate arrest under PMLA unless you pay money to verify your Aadhaar.
- Defense Rule: DoT and TRAI NEVER disconnect phone numbers via automated calls or ask you to press 9. If you receive such a call, hang up immediately. Check your registered mobile connections on the official Sanchar Saathi (sancharsaathi.gov.in) portal or dial 1930.
- Statutory Authority: DoT & Sanchar Saathi Advisory (https://sancharsaathi.gov.in/)

### Scam #12: The FedEx / DHL "Drugs Found in International Courier" Threat
- Platform: Phone Call / Video Call
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: An automated call claiming to be FedEx or DHL claims: "A courier parcel sent using your Aadhaar to Taiwan or Cambodia containing MDMA drugs, fake passports, and illegal debit cards was intercepted by customs." The call is transferred to fake "Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB)" or "Mumbai Crime Branch" officers over video call who demand financial statements and emergency escrow transfers.
- Defense Rule: Courier companies like FedEx and DHL never transfer customer calls to police or narcotics agencies. Police never interrogate suspects or demand security deposits over video calls. Hang up, block, and dial 1930.
- Statutory Authority: I4C & Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) Advisory (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #13: The Deepfake Government Welfare & PM Yojana Ads
- Platform: Instagram / Facebook / YouTube
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: Sponsored video ads on Facebook, Instagram, or YouTube feature hyper-realistic AI deepfakes of government leaders and ministers announcing instant "₹5,000 festive relief funds" or "free smartphone subsidies". Clicking the link directs you to an unauthorized portal that triggers a UPI Collect Request (which debits your account) or installs banking malware.
- Defense Rule: Government welfare schemes are never disbursed via social media ads or UPI collect requests. Entering your UPI PIN always DEDUCTS money from your bank account. Verify official government schemes only on .gov.in portals.
- Statutory Authority: I4C National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #14: The Fake Google Customer Care & Screen Share Hijack
- Platform: Google Search / WhatsApp Video
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: When searching for Swiggy, Zomato, IRCTC, or bank customer support on Google, users dial a fake number placed by scammers. The fake agent says: "To process your ₹200 refund, share your screen on WhatsApp video call or install AnyDesk/QuickSupport." Once screen sharing starts, the scammer initiates a bank transfer and reads the incoming OTP directly off the live screen.
- Defense Rule: Never search for customer service phone numbers on Google Search; always use the in-app help section. Never share your mobile screen or accept screen-sharing requests during a customer support call.
- Statutory Authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI Sachet Advisory) (https://sachet.rbi.org.in/)

### Scam #15: The Corporate Tax & MCA Notice Archive Trap (Infostealer ZIP)
- Platform: Email / WhatsApp
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: Accountants, CAs, company directors, and finance personnel receive an urgent email or WhatsApp: "Statutory notice regarding pending tax filing discrepancies / MCA audit. Attached: Statement_of_Account.zip or MCA_Notice.zip." Extracting the file runs a disguised Windows executable that quietly exfiltrates corporate net banking tokens, DSC credentials, and browser passwords.
- Defense Rule: Tax authorities and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) never send audit notices as compressed .zip or .rar files via WhatsApp or personal email. Check all corporate filings directly on the official mca.gov.in portal.
- Statutory Authority: I4C Corporate Threat Advisory & CERT-In (https://www.cert-in.org.in/)

### Scam #16: The Pensioner "Digital Life Certificate / Jeevan Pramaan" KYC Scam
- Platform: Phone Call / WhatsApp
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: Fraudsters call senior citizens posing as bank or pension disbursement officers: "Your annual digital life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan) is expiring today. Your pension will stop next month unless verified right now." The caller asks for Aadhaar OTPs or asks them to install a remote-access app to "scan their face", instantly draining the pensioner's life savings.
- Defense Rule: Pension authorities never call to ask for Aadhaar OTPs or banking passwords to submit Jeevan Pramaan. Senior citizens should submit life certificates only via the official Jeevan Pramaan Face App or in person at bank branches or post offices.
- Statutory Authority: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions & I4C (https://cybercrime.gov.in/)

### Scam #17: The Airport Lounge & Credit Card Points Phishing Link
- Platform: SMS / Web Clone
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You receive an SMS: "Your complimentary airport lounge access and reward points expire tonight. Re-verify your card benefits immediately: [shortened link]". The link opens a cloned DreamFolks/bank webpage asking for card number, CVV, expiry, and OTP, allowing fraudsters to make high-value international transactions.
- Defense Rule: Banks and airport lounge operators never send SMS links threatening sudden cancellation of lounge privileges. Never enter card CVV or OTPs on links received via SMS. Check card benefits directly in your bank's official app.
- Statutory Authority: CERT-In Financial Phishing Advisory (https://www.cert-in.org.in/)

### Scam #18: The Fake Courier Delivery / Incomplete Address Trap
- Platform: SMS / Web Clone
- Severity: HIGH
- The Trap: You receive an SMS from "India Post" or "Courier": "Your package cannot be delivered due to an incomplete house number. Update your address within 24 hours or parcel will be returned." The link opens an India Post cloned webpage asking for a ₹25 redelivery fee, harvesting your debit card number and OTP.
- Defense Rule: India Post never sends SMS links asking for fee payments to correct addresses. Track parcels only using the tracking number directly on the official indiapost.gov.in website.
- Statutory Authority: India Post & PIB Fact Check (https://www.indiapost.gov.in/)

### Scam #19: The Bogus Stock Market "VIP Institutional IPO" Group
- Platform: WhatsApp / Fake App
- Severity: CRITICAL
- The Trap: You are added to a WhatsApp group named after a famous global brokerage. "Mentors" promise guaranteed 100% allocation in blockbuster IPOs and instruct you to trade through a customized app. The app shows massive fake profits, but when you attempt to withdraw, they demand a 20% "tax release fee" and freeze your account.
- Defense Rule: SEBI-registered brokerages never conduct institutional IPO bidding or accept investments via WhatsApp groups. Never deposit money into personal accounts for stock market trading.
- Statutory Authority: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (https://www.sebi.gov.in/)


---

## 3. Emergency Golden Hour Protocol for Financial Fraud
1. Call 1930 (National Cyber Crime Helpline) within 2 hours.
2. Screenshot all chats, transaction reference numbers (UTR), and caller IDs.
3. Submit e-FIR on https://cybercrime.gov.in.
4. Deliver dispute letter with complaint acknowledgement to your bank branch within 24 hours.
